anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L1 Simplified mine asks the agent to rotate among four fixed viewpoints, click frontmost exposed faces, preserve supports, and extract a small target set. The d1 Simplified apothecary already requires choosing among three jars and five curvature outcomes at two sequential route rings, matching both center and heading, then recovering or finishing at a target effect. It is a materially richer 2D decision problem even though its controls are discrete.

evidence.explanation: The anchor generates a fixed 5x5x3 raycast mine with target, durability, support and lava constraints.
The simplified anchor uses rotation buttons and canvas clicks; the full drag surface is separate.
The anchor grader replays exact view, ray-hit, durability, support and extraction state.
The d1 profile has three ingredients, two commits, five notches, broad reveal, no vortex and a wide target.
A route ring accepts a candidate only when its path is within the fixed center and heading tolerances.

anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L3 Full board has an autonomously ticking physical state: momentum, friction, walls, wells, ordered lamps and a cup. Apothecary d2 Full has less autonomous motion but adds four exact state-dependent route commitments, six-by-nine visible candidate combinations, fog-limited information, a vortex recovery branch, and duration-based grinding plus a physical jar transfer. The d2 Full task is at least L3 and, in this source-only comparison, sits near the L4 boundary.

evidence.explanation: The anchor's L3 baseline geometry and physics include three lamps, walls, wells, 50 ms ticks, and minimum replay requirements.
Each anchor tick updates velocity, position, collisions, hazards, ordered lamp progress and cup completion.
The anchor grader replays the full time-ordered physics transcript and requires ticks, controls, ordered lamps and completion.
The current d2 profile has four commits, six ingredients, nine notches, one vortex and narrowed reveal/target geometry.
Full grinding advances one notch per 240 ms and route motion changes position and future gate state only after each stir.

anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L4 Full courier requires a 48-to-105-roll route through barriers while maintaining cube orientation, satisfying gate face constraints, and using sparse scanners when orientation is hidden. Apothecary d2 Full has fewer repeated moves and exposes a geometric preview, but its four dependent rings, fog, exact center/heading match, and full jar/pestle controls put it close to that L4 decision-and-control burden. D3 and above are clearly no easier than this anchor on source evidence.

evidence.explanation: The anchor creates barrier gates with face requirements, scanner visibility choices and bounded long solution routes.
The visible anchor hides orientation outside the initial reveal and scanner cells while tracking gate crossings.
The anchor grader replays every move, orientation roll, gate condition and final ordered delivery.
Apothecary previews a candidate path and tests both center and heading against the current ring.

anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L5 Simplified candy task requires an exact score over four valid swaps, with each accepted swap changing the later board through cascades and a forbidden candy that voids the run. Apothecary d5 Simplified has five dependent route commits, fifteen close curve outcomes, tight fog, three vortices, eight bones with zero tolerated contact, six effects and an 18 pixel target. It is comparable to L5 in exactness and changing-state planning, while d4 Simplified is a plausible L4 comparison.

evidence.explanation: The anchor searches for a four-swap route whose later boards and cascade waves produce one exact target score.
Each valid swap changes the board and refill cursor; a forbidden swap or wrong final receipt terminates the run.
The anchor grader independently replays the state-changing swap transcript and exact score requirement.
Apothecary d5 retains five commits while tightening notches, reveal, target radius and hazard tolerance.

visible_baseline_solution: A screenshot-only agent sees the ordered effect name and glyph in the header, the 2D map with an origin, fog-revealed region, the current route ring, visible map geometry and a cabinet of six labeled jars. It must choose a jar, put it in the mortar, and inspect the colored path preview while selecting one of nine curve notches until the preview reaches the current ring with the correct heading. In Full, the jar must be physically dragged into the mortar and the pestle must be held for the required 240 ms notch ticks; in Simplified, the jar and notch are selected by clicks. Clicking STIR PATH advances the path in four six-sample chunks, reveals the wake, and commits the route only if the path was aligned and did not hit a vortex. The agent repeats this dependent process for four rings, avoiding visible and newly revealed bones and vortices. A wrong probe can be recovered with the visible water and bellows controls within their budgets, but a clean solve does not need to spend them. Finally it must bring the flask into the effect disc identified by the order and press SEAL exactly once. The grader requires the event transcript, final position and heading, route progress, target effect, hazard limit and resource budgets to replay exactly.

baseline_judgment.rationale: The current d2/full configuration is not a convincing L2 task when the complete screenshot-only control problem is counted. It has four state-dependent route decisions, a six-by-nine candidate space per ring, narrow center and heading tolerances, fog, hidden hazards, a vortex recovery branch, and full drag plus duration-based grinding. It is richer than the approved L1 mine and at least comparable to the approved L3 Gyroscopic Tilt Board; its four exact route commitments and full interaction place it near the approved L4 Blind Dice Courier. The source-only estimate is therefore L4, with a possible L3-L4 boundary pending calibration. Because the current default uses the same parameters as d2, changing only the baseline number would break the controllability plan's fixed-seed baseline correspondence; the exact default profile would need to be moved or copied to the proposed level.

evidence.explanation: The current baseline is d2/full/live and the d2 profile is explicitly the six-jar, four-commit, nine-notch configuration.
Grinding changes constant-curvature geometry and a route ring requires a unique ingredient/notch pair under center and heading tolerances.
The visible map is fogged and only the traveled trace opens it; candidate previews, hazards and the current route ring are rendered on the map.
Full mode adds physical jar loading and 240 ms duration-based grinding, while each stir changes the route state.
The hidden route is required to uniquely match each visible ring and terminate at the requested effect without obstruction.
Full jar loading is independently checked for visible start/end rectangles, travel and pointer samples.

uncertainties: No human or computer-use-agent calibration was run in this source review, so the L3-versus-L4 boundary is a source comparison rather than a measured threshold.

The comparison counts a clean screenshot-only solution and treats the generated recovery branch as an active error-recovery affordance; its practical value depends on how often agents make wrong commits.

profiles.success_condition: Use simplified selection and notch controls, complete four exact unobstructed commits and reach/seal the requested effect under the d3 hazard and recovery budgets.

baseline_preservation.current_default_equivalence: The no-condition generator path uses BASELINE_PARAMETERS, whose values exactly match the explicit d2 parameters in controls.json. At a fixed seed and equivalent base task identity, the generated world geometry, route, hazards, effects, mechanics and interaction geometry therefore use the same parameters. The controlled materializer changes task IDs and adds the control condition, so challenge identity metadata is intentionally different even when the world parameters match.
baseline_preservation.historical_preservation: Unknown. The supplied source contains the current default generator and controlled profiles but no historical pre-controls generator, commit, fixture or archived generated state for this environment.

evidence.explanation: The default path returns BASELINE_PARAMETERS while controlled generation reads difficulty_parameters from the condition.

Controlled tasks receive new IDs and copy the selected profile into metadata without changing the generator implementation.
The explicit d2 object contains the same values as BASELINE_PARAMETERS.

missing_evidence: No historical pre-controls source or fixed-seed artifact was supplied, so semantic preservation from an earlier implementation cannot be established.

interaction_equivalence.comparison_assessment: No world or goal compromise found. The pair intentionally differs in motor/timing demand, so Full is harder as an interaction configuration even though the resulting ingredient and grind state effects are the same.

interaction_equivalence.comparison_assessment: The d2 comparison is valid for world difficulty. Full adds a real gesture and duration-control burden, so it should not be treated as behaviorally identical to Simplified in measured interaction difficulty.

findings.claim: gate_radius is a visual ring-size parameter, not the actual route-alignment tolerance.
findings.causal_explanation: The generator stores each profile's gate_radius on the drawn ring. Browser preview alignment and grader alignment instead use fixed mechanics.gate_center_tolerance 2.25 and gate_heading_tolerance_degrees 2.0. Changing gate_radius therefore changes the visual affordance but not the accepted center/heading error; the d1-to-d5 shrinking gate sizes do not establish a corresponding control difficulty increase.

evidence.explanation: gate_radius is copied into the visible route-ring record.
Preview alignment uses mechanics gate center/heading tolerances, not the ring radius.
Independent grading likewise receives fixed center and heading tolerance values.

findings.recommended_action: Do not credit gate_radius as an independent difficulty lever. Either remove it from profile rationale or make the mechanics tolerances intentionally derive from it, with matching browser and grader behavior.

findings.claim: Ingredient, water and bellows budgets are active recovery constraints but do not make a clean solution harder by themselves.
findings.causal_explanation: A clean generated solution uses one ingredient per route commit and avoids water/bellows; these resources matter when an agent commits a wrong route or contacts a vortex and tries to recover. The generator intentionally creates a recoverable wrong probe, and the browser/grader implement bounded recovery, so the parameters are real but conditional rather than independent base-route difficulty.

evidence.explanation: The recovery probe is deliberately selected to be recoverable within the configured water/bellows reserve.
Recovery actions only run when no ingredient path is active and consume their respective budgets.
The grader treats water/bellows as optional bounded events and replays them only if present.
Budgets are active pass limits, but no minimum recovery spend is required.

findings.recommended_action: Retain the recovery affordance, but describe these values as error-recovery capacity and do not use their numerical monotonicity alone to justify adjacent difficulty levels.

findings.claim: The current d2/full baseline appears underlabelled relative to the approved cross-environment references.
findings.causal_explanation: The current source profile combines four changing route decisions, fog, hidden hazards and exact geometric alignment with full drag/timed controls. That is materially above the approved L1 mine, at least L3-like, and close to the approved L4 courier. This source estimate places it at L4, but the d4 profile is not parameter-equivalent to the current default, so a baseline relabel requires profile reassignment to preserve fixed-seed equivalence.

evidence.explanation: The baseline is d2/full while d2 contains the original six-jar/four-ring/full-interface configuration.
Approved anchors place Isometric Voxel Extraction Mine at L1, Gyroscopic Tilt Board at L3, Blind Dice Courier at L4 and Exact-Change Candy Cascade at L5.
All route rings must uniquely match and the hidden route must reach the target without obstruction.

findings.recommended_action: Run the planned fixed-seed and calibrated human/agent comparisons before final adjudication; if the source estimate is confirmed, move/copy the current default parameters into the chosen baseline profile and re-place the other profiles around it.

verdict.concise_summary: The source supports an ordered d1-to-d5 ladder, but d2/full is likely L4-scale rather than L2. D1 is a low discrete route task, d2 is a fogged four-decision task, d3 is a tighter same-stage variant, d4 adds a dependent stage and vortex, and d5 activates the strongest precision and hazard constraints. gate_radius is visual-only, and resource budgets primarily govern recovery. The current default matches explicit d2 parameters, so any baseline relabel must also revise profile placement to preserve fixed-seed equivalence.
limitations: This is source-only analysis; no browser, multi-seed generation, grader, exported-verifier, VNC or human calibration checks were performed.
The L3/L4 and L4/L5 boundaries are comparative estimates against approved anchors, not measured pass-rate thresholds.
Historical pre-controls implementation evidence is unavailable.
